Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B
Q2: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: I confirmed the gap in `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` `classify_runner_shutdown` (lines 330-404). When `lint` is the only `failure` job, the code adds nothing to `shutdown_ids`. The aggregate loop (lines 394-402) accepts the `cancelled` jobs that `lint` names, but line 403 still returns `"unverified"`, which is logged as `runner_shutdown_unverified` (lines 517/525). So the sweep can never re-run this case today. Option A is out because it needs someone to close the issue and re-run CI by hand, which goes against the automation-bias rule (§20) and the pipeline-capability rule. Option C would also edit the `lint` gate in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, but the triage itself says that gate is working as designed and should stay unchanged. B is the narrowest change that recovers this case automatically.
Q2: The medium rule matches how the script already treats shutdowns. At lines 361-363 a job counts only if every failure annotation is `RUNNER_SHUTDOWN_PREFIX` or `SHUTDOWN_COMPANION_MESSAGE` ("The operation was canceled."). That rule catches runners lost partway through a job, which strict misses, and it still treats a `timeout-minutes` cancellation as a real failure, which loose would not.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1 / Q2 (letter decisions, binding constraints for the planner):
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py (`classify_runner_shutdown` lines 330-404, `failure_annotations` line 311, `RUNNER_SHUTDOWN_PREFIX` line 45, `SHUTDOWN_COMPANION_MESSAGE` line 81, `MAX_FAILED_JOBS_CLASSIFIED = 10` line 83, env parsing around lines 113 and 554)
    - .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml line 603 (where `CI_CHECKOUT_FETCH_RERUN_ENABLED` is wired with `vars.... || 'true'`)
    - tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py (the existing contract tests)
    - README.md variables table (the row for `CI_CHECKOUT_FETCH_RERUN_ENABLED`, line 152)
  steps:
    - Add a new class to `classify_runner_shutdown`, for example the return value `"abandoned"`, plus a keyword parameter that defaults to enabled. It applies only when all of these hold:
      - the only `failure` job is `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB_NAME` (`lint`);
      - the aggregate's annotations pass the existing checks at lines 382-393;
      - every non-skipped, non-success job that the aggregate message names is `cancelled`;
      - each of those `cancelled` jobs passes the Q2 medium test.
    - Q2 medium test: read the job's failure annotations with the existing `failure_annotations` helper. The job counts as abandoned only if every annotation is `RUNNER_SHUTDOWN_PREFIX` or exactly `SHUTDOWN_COMPANION_MESSAGE`; no annotations also counts. Any other annotation, including the timeout text "has exceeded the maximum execution time", returns `"genuine"`. Do not log annotation text; follow the existing rule at line 343.
    - Fail closed on the API budget. Count these extra annotation reads against `MAX_FAILED_JOBS_CLASSIFIED`. If the named `cancelled` jobs plus the failed jobs exceed that cap, return `"unverified"`. If annotations can't be read (`annotations_unreadable`), return `"unverified"`. Update the docstring's "No extra API reads" line to describe the new bounded reads.
    - Route the new class through the same re-run path and the same once-per-head re-run cap as `checkout_fetch`. Emit a distinct decision reason so the logs can tell it apart.
    - Add the off switch env var `CI_ABANDONED_JOB_RERUN_ENABLED`. The name is not used anywhere in the repo yet. Default it to `true` in the script itself (§8), parse it like `CI_CHECKOUT_FETCH_RERUN_ENABLED` (warn on a bad value, keep the default), and when it is `false` keep today's `"unverified"` outcome.
    - Wire it in `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml` next to line 603: `CI_ABANDONED_JOB_RERUN_ENABLED: ${{ vars.CI_ABANDONED_JOB_RERUN_ENABLED || 'true' }}`. Add a README variables-table row.
    - Add contract tests in tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py:
      - only `lint` failed and the named jobs are `cancelled` with only cancel/shutdown annotations or none: classified as abandoned and re-run;
      - a named `cancelled` job has a timeout annotation: `"genuine"`;
      - a named `cancelled` job has any other annotation: `"genuine"`;
      - switch set to `false`: `"unverified"`;
      - too many `cancelled` jobs for the cap: `"unverified"`;
      - a second abandoned run on the same head: blocked by the once-per-head cap.
    - Do not change the `lint` aggregate job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Leave the Copilot `custom_instructions_too_large` problem out of scope.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: n/a
  reversibility: Set the repo variable `CI_ABANDONED_JOB_RERUN_ENABLED=false` to get today's behaviour back (`runner_shutdown_unverified`, no re-run). The change only adds code, so reverting it is safe.
